Why can't you make the existing code work? 

chassis 1 cooled_by fan 1 
chassis 1 cooled_by fan 2

chassis 2 cooled_by fan 1 
chassis 2 cooled_by fan 2

...

Because redfish resources can't be present underneath multiple URIs.

The `cooling/cooled_by` directly determines resource placement currently.

So we would have something like

```
redfish/v1/Chassis/Yv3_Chassis_1/ThermalSubsystem/Fans/FAN_1
redfish/v1/Chassis/Yv3_Chassis_1/ThermalSubsystem/Fans/FAN_2

redfish/v1/Chassis/Yv3_Chassis_2/ThermalSubsystem/Fans/FAN_1
redfish/v1/Chassis/Yv3_Chassis_2/ThermalSubsystem/Fans/FAN_2
```

Which is not allowed in redfish from my understanding.

An alternative would be to use `cooling/cooled_by` for the resource placement as before and yet another association to determine which chassis the fan is actually cooling.

But that's conceptually wrong since bmcweb conventionally uses `containing` association to determine resource placement and the  `cooling` association describes a concept that's not `1:1`.

It's more like an `1:n` where one fan can be cooling multiple things.

So if we were to continue with the existing code it would be conceptually inconsistent in bmcweb and require introducing yet another association.

> Which is not allowed in redfish from my understanding.

Can you quote the spec here ? 
I don't read below to mean you can't do this: 
"'The service root and resource path component parts uniquely identify the resource in a Redfish service.`."

### my spec interpretation

> Can you quote the spec here ?
  I don't read below to mean you can't do this:

I believe you already found the most relevant section in the spec.

`redfish/v1/Chassis/Yv3_Chassis_1/ThermalSubsystem/Fans/FAN_1`

has service root `redfish/v1` and resource path `Chassis/Yv3_Chassis_1/ThermalSubsystem/Fans/FAN_1`.

quoting from redfish spec:

If we had 2 URIs refer to the same physical fan (FAN_1) like
```
redfish/v1/Chassis/Yv3_Chassis_1/ThermalSubsystem/Fans/FAN_1
redfish/v1/Chassis/Yv3_Chassis_2/ThermalSubsystem/Fans/FAN_1```

then the URI would not uniquely identify the resource anymore.

Another section from the spec:
```
A Universal Resource Identifier (URI) identifies a resource, including the service root and all Redfish resources.
• A URI shall identify each unique instance of a resource.
```

I interpret
```
The service root and resource path component parts
uniquely identify the resource in a Redfish service.
```
to mean that from the URI alone we know which one it is and there is no need for the client to de-duplicate copies of it.

If aliases were allowed to exist, i would expect wording like
`The service root and resource path component parts **identify** the resource
in a Redfish service.` (without the additional word "**uniquely**")

### HTTP Redirect

The spec contains a section on HTTP Redirects

```
6.3 HTTP redirect
HTTP redirect enables a service to redirect a request to another URL. Among other things, HTTP redirect enables
Redfish resources to alias areas of the data model.
All Redfish clients shall correctly handle HTTP redirect.
```

And i assume it's okay to use them, but we still require one real instance to redirect to. So we would need to know which links redirect (`cooling`) and where the real resource is (`containing`). 

I have not seen redirects used extensively in bmcweb. I would prefer to not use them here since it introduces extra round-trips and indirection for the redfish client.



### summary of problems caused by allowing copies of a resource

- redfish client now has to do a full query on all instances of a resource to know how many instances actually exist

- redfish client has to implement deduplication logic for resources to know which ones are copies (AFAIK there exists no implementation yet to do this)

- since different copies of the same resources may be fetched at different times,
  the response content may be different even if the refer to the same resource, making deduplication even harder

- deduplication of copies is only possible if there are properties like serial number or other unique identifier

- redfish client must choose one of the copy of the resource if it wants to do PATCH/POST request. It's not clear which one to choose?

- `RelatedItem` also becomes less clear. Do we list all copies of a resource here or just one of them ? If we list one, which one is it?

### summary of problems caused by using HTTP redirects (alias)

- redfish client now has to do a full query on all instances of a resource to know how many instances actually exist

- redirects have to be resolved before `PATCH/POST` ?

- What do we put in `RelatedItem`? Do we put the link to the real resource or the alias?

### my opinion

From my perspective an interpretation of redfish spec allowing copies of a resource on a different resource path is less useful to a Redfish client.

> then the URI would not uniquely identify the resource anymore.

Yeah I believe so too. These two URIs now uniquely identify **two distinct** fans, that both happen to be called 'FAN_1' as I understand. 

Redfish seem to allow for that since both URIs are unique, however we don't describe what we intend to describe..considering these are two distinct resources from a Redfish perspective, I wonder if we breach the odata uniqueness of odata@id then? 

> So if we were to continue with the existing code it would be 
conceptually inconsistent in bmcweb and require introducing yet another 
association.

I agree, it would be more consistent with the spec using 'containing/contained_by' to determine the correct ThermalSubsystem FanCollection, and 'cooling/cooled_by' to determine the correct `CoolingChassis` arrays.
